add: reusable playbooks for reporting and analysis

add: add an existing MCP server to the agent
confirm the agent cannot exceed approved actions
why: The dropped phrase is a generic security test that fits every access set-up service (EP01, FR01, GS01 all test access). The phrases were also missing connecting an existing tool by adding it as a server, which is this service's own work (new MCP servers are excluded). The second add keeps the negative test but ties it to the agent.

why: An RFI usually words this work as moving off the current CMS, and the set had no phrase for that.

integration architecture for the new site

why: Templates and social publishing point to EP03 and EP06, whose phrases already cover deciding who may publish and template control. Seven role and Manager Hub phrases remain.

add: train managers on template sharing settings
why: Without the training angle, the phrase reads as setting up template sharing (EP03). The rewrite keeps it as training.

drop: set up Firefly custom model access
projects to store and share custom models

drop: publish custom model for use in Photoshop
why: The first dropped phrase implies a claim about which Adobe apps can use a published model. The second is the outcome of the whole Custom Models product and fits FM01 to FM07 alike. The add keeps publishing tied to this service's testing.

add: assign Firefly Services licenses to groups
user groups for creative automation access
why: Author and runner roles point to FP08's operating rules ("who authors, publishes and runs workflows"). Consumption tracking against an entitlement is generic and points to FP09's monthly Operations report. The adds cover the Admin Console assignment this service owns.

drop: process thousands of images at once
why: A volume phrase with no preset action in it. It fits FP05's API batch runs as well. Seven phrases about the specific presets remain.

drop: creative lead sign-off on workflow outputs
why: Creative lead sign-off is also FP10's step and close to FP04's refining to the brief. Starting from Adobe's workflow templates is what sets this service apart, and no phrase said so.

add: decide who gets admin access to all content
why: Adding and removing users is FR08's monthly scope word for word. FR01 keeps its procedure phrases (onboarding and offboarding, joiner and leaver), and the add covers the Content Admin decision.
As written, this is a product capability question, so a question about whether Frame.io supports time-stamped feedback would wrongly land on a training service. The rewrite keeps it as training.
